newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA THRASH ENGLAND TO DEPRESS ROWELL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA THRASH ENGLAND TO DEPRESS ROWELL.

text.p: Australia brought England's contingent of triumphant British Lions down to earth with a convincing 25-6 win in a one-off rugby union test on Saturday.
The Wallabies ran in four tries without reply at the Sydney Football Stadium to depress England coach Jack Rowell's spirits in what could prove to be his last match in charge.
Australia dominated for virtually the whole match against a side featuring 12 players who helped the Lions to secure a 2-1 series win against South Africa last week.

Despite their overwhelming superiority, the home side led only 8-6 early in the second half before winger Ben Tune, scrum-half George Gregan and fly-half Tim Horan scored tries to add some realism to the scoreline.
It was Horan's first try since his switch from the centres by Wallaby coach Greg Smith this season.
The margin of victory would have been even greater but for a mediocre kicking display by Australia captain and lock John Eales, who missed one conversion and three penalty attempts.
Rowell, whose contract expires next month, saw his team defend resolutely but offer little threat in attack in front of a crowd of just over 40,000.
The visitors relied on the accurate kicking of fly-half Mike Catt, who landed a penalty and a drop goal either side of half-time.
Full-back Matt Burke, who missed Australia's last three test matches because of a groin strain, made a telling impact on his return by scoring the opening try after 12 minutes.
Horan began the move with a cut-out pass to winger Joe Roff, who came into the line to find a gap in the centres before releasing Burke into the open.
Burke, Australia's regular goal-kicker, added to his points tally with one conversion after taking from Eales in the second half.

England - 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-John Bentley, 13-Phil de Glanville (captain), 12-Nick Greenstock, 11-Nick Beal; 10-Mike Catt, 9-Matthew Dawson (16-Austin Healy, 40th); 8-Tim Rodber, 7-Richard Hill (21-Ben Clarke, 69th), 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Nigel Redman, 3-Darren Garforth, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.

Australia - 15-Matthew Burke; 14-Joe Roff, 13-Jason Little, 12-James Holbeck, 11-Ben Tune; 10-Tim Horan, 9-George Gregan; 8-Troy Coker (19-Matt Cockbain, 36th), 7-Brett Robinson, 6-Daniel Manu, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Garrick Morgan, 3-Cameron Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Ewen McKenzie (20-Andrew Blades, 65th).
